location: New London police station parking lot, New London, Connecticut
inciting_reason: Self-described first amendment auditor Daniel Kokoszka (YouTube channel 'Constitution State') filmed at the police station parking lot; three separate officer encounters were recorded

key_facts.fact: The city released the body camera footage from multiple officers together with its internal investigation in response to a Freedom of Information request from The Day, New London's daily newspaper.
key_facts.citation: The Day, 'First Amendment audit leads to suspension of New London cop' (Apr 8, 2023)

key_facts.fact: The body camera footage shows Lt. Joshua Bergeson blocking and pushing auditor Daniel Kokoszka in an attempt to force him to leave the parking lot.
The internal investigation concluded with an eight-day suspension and mandated retraining for Lt. Bergeson.
Bergeson was cited for violating department policy on 'respect and courtesy,' 'conduct unbecoming an officer,' and 'use of force reporting.'
key_facts.citation: Police1, 'First Amendment audit leads to suspension of Conn. officer'

key_facts.fact: State's Attorney Paul Narducci determined there were no violations of criminal statutes in the encounter.
Complaints against Sgt. Ryan Linderson, Ofc. Michael Lewis, Ofc. Eric Sadowski, and Lt. Lawrence Keating were found unfounded.
The local police union filed a grievance seeking to overturn Bergeson's suspension.
On July 6, 2021, Police Chief Brian Wright sent a memo to officers about First Amendment rights.
Bergeson had previously been fired in 2011 for absenteeism and was rehired a year later.

verdict_outcome: Administrative discipline, verified: eight-day suspension and mandated retraining for Lt. Joshua Bergeson following the city's internal investigation; the State's Attorney found no criminal violations; the police union filed a grievance seeking to overturn the suspension. No criminal charges were filed.
